macro.headline: Indices above trend but momentum fading — transitional tape, not euphoric, not washed out.
macro.story:
The headline indices are still above their 50- and 200-day moving averages, but underneath the surface momentum is fading. SPY closed at 737.76 with RSI at a neutral 50.3, MACD has rolled below its signal line, and the 5-day change is -2.55% — price is holding the uptrend, but the buyers have lost the initiative. QQQ tells the same story: above both moving averages, but RSI 53.6 with MACD negative and a -3.17% week. The Dow and Russell are relatively firmer, with breadth quietly broadening into small-caps and cyclicals rather than mega-cap tech leading.

The dominant cross-asset catalyst grounded in the active themes is the AI Infrastructure capex cycle, which the theme data flags as CHASING-stage and funded by an unwind of macro hedges. That fingerprint is visible right here in the data: gold is down ~10% over 21 days and silver down ~24.5% with both below their 50- and 200-day moving averages, while DXY is grinding higher (RSI 60, above both SMAs, MACD positive). That's the validated dollar-strength-versus-metals inverse relationship doing its job — capital is leaving inflation hedges. But the AI bid itself looks tired here, with Technology sector status WEAK and Nasdaq 100 status WEAK, suggesting the CHASING theme is mid-correction even if not invalidated.

Defensive leadership is the tell. Healthcare and Consumer Staples are the two HOT sectors with the highest momentum scores, joined by Financials and Real Estate. That is not the rotation pattern of a market about to launch — it's the pattern of a market protecting gains while the growth complex digests. VIX at 19.03 is down 11.5% on the week but still up 10.2% over 21 days, and VIX3M is in contango — fear has eased from a recent spike, but term structure is no longer pricing complacency. The yield curve (10Y-2Y) has flattened sharply, -28% over 21 days, which is a quiet warning underneath an otherwise calm tape.

Net-net: this is a transitional regime. Engine C is CALM (no washout to trade), and breadth/sentiment are neither stretched nor extreme. Stay selective — hunt longs inside the validated Early-Runway industries where rotation tailwinds are confirmed, and respect that the macro is not offering a clean directional edge right now.

newsletter:
**[THE SPINE]** The AI infrastructure trade is the dominant force on the tape this week, and it's bifurcating into a two-tier market. XLK is +6.6% over 21 days with accelerating bullish trajectory, Semiconductors are up 8.5% on the month, and Software-Infrastructure just flipped to ACCELERATING_BULLISH at +6.7%. Everything else — financials, healthcare, real estate — is positive but secondary. The AI Infrastructure theme is in CHASING stage at day 14 with health 8/10, which tells you the spine is intact but the easy money in the leaders is behind us.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The macro backdrop is permissive, not euphoric. Regime is CHOPPY at 6/10 confidence with breadth a healthy 72.7% above 50SMA and S&P 5-day breadth bullish 61% vs bearish 16%. VIX at 16.6 in contango with VIX3M at 20.5 is the textbook risk-on term structure. SPY RSI 59.9 is trending — not a fade (overbought-fade has zero edge in our work). The one active macro signal is DXY_METALS_TAG: dollar is above both 21d and 50d SMAs, and that's the durable headwind keeping Gold (-6.3% 21d), Silver (-16.2%), and the entire Precious Metals theme in FADING status. 10Y at 4.45% drifted lower this week but we don't trade a yield ceiling — that signal doesn't hold. Oil at $80, RSI 33.7, down 20.6% on the month is in a downtrend, full stop — no mean-reversion edge there.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into Consumer Electronics, Software-Infrastructure, and unspecified industry buckets — all AI-adjacent. Nothing has rotated OUT in the formal flip list, which means this is additive flow, not a defensive rotation. XLF (+4.9%) and IWM (+4.3%) riding shotgun is constructive: financials and small caps participating means the rally has legs beyond just mega-cap compute. XLP at +0.5% is the laggard, confirming defensive demand is absent. The fading themes — Precious Metals and Broad Commodities — are funding sources, not warning lights.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The leaders have already run and you need to be honest about where you are on each. Semiconductors are HOT for 13 months, +258% — that is the maximum on record, ceiling territory; historically these spells have near-zero median remaining gain, so this is an exit-management problem, not an entry. Semiconductor Equipment & Materials is the same story at +288% over 12 months. Where the runway actually exists: Software-Infrastructure is HOT only 1 month with just +3% gain so far against a typical +18% — early innings of an accelerating move (names like MSFT, ORCL, PANW, NOW deserve attention). Internet Content & Information also flipped HOT at month 1 with -5% gain — earlier than typical, with room. Internet Retail is choppy but with bullish trajectory at +9.4% (AMZN). The UN-RUN screen came back empty today, which itself is a tell: the coil-and-pop names have already broken out.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY 98.88 support. As long as the dollar holds its 21d/50d uptrend, the metals fade persists and dollar-funded risk assets stay bid. A clean break of DXY 98.88 would invalidate the active macro signal, likely re-rate Gold/Silver/Copper higher, and signal the AI-led growth bid is sharing oxygen with a reflation trade. On the equity side, SPY 760.4 resistance is the level — through it cleanly and the CHOPPY regime resolves bullish; rejection sets up a retest of 731.5. Remember the discipline: any washout low we get from here is statistically retested within 60 days 88% of the time — never call a bottom on one bounce.
